points.title: 童年与教育
points.description: 克尔凯郭尔出生于哥本哈根一个富裕的商人家庭，父亲迈克尔·彼得森·克尔凯郭尔曾是羊绒商人，后成为地主。童年时期，克尔凯郭尔与家人经历了多次悲剧，包括五个兄弟姐妹的早逝。这种家庭背景深刻影响了他后来的哲学思考。他接受了良好的教育，在哥本哈根的私立学校学习，展现出非凡的智力天赋，但也因体弱多病而经常被排除在同龄人的社交活动之外。这段时期，他开始对宗教和人生意义产生深刻思考，为日后的哲学创作奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Kierkegaard was born in Copenhagen into a wealthy merchant family. His father, Michael Pedersen Kierkegaard, had been a wool merchant before becoming a landowner. During his childhood, Kierkegaard experienced multiple tragedies within his family, including the early deaths of five of his siblings. This family background profoundly influenced his later philosophical thinking. He received an excellent education at private schools in Copenhagen, showing remarkable intellectual talent, but was often excluded from peer social activities due to poor health. During this period, he began to develop deep thoughts about religion and the meaning of life, laying the foundation for his future philosophical works.

points.title: 大学时期与早期创作
points.description: 1830年，克尔凯郭尔进入哥本哈根大学，最初学习神学，后转向哲学和文学。他深受黑格尔哲学的影响，但逐渐对其体系化、抽象化的方法产生怀疑。1837年，他与雷吉娜·奥尔森(Regine Olsen)相遇并坠入爱河，1838年订婚。然而，出于对婚姻的哲学思考和对'世俗生活'的恐惧，他在1841年突然解除婚约，这一决定成为他一生中最大的个人悲剧之一，也深刻影响了他后来的创作。1841年，他完成博士论文《论反讽的概念》，获得博士学位，但随即前往柏林继续学习，师从谢林。
points.descriptionEn: In 1830, Kierkegaard entered the University of Copenhagen, initially studying theology before turning to philosophy and literature. He was deeply influenced by Hegelian philosophy but gradually became skeptical of its systematic and abstract methods. In 1837, he met and fell in love with Regine Olsen, becoming engaged in 1838. However, due to philosophical reflections on marriage and fear of 'secular life', he abruptly broke off the engagement in 1841, which became one of the greatest personal tragedies of his life and profoundly influenced his later work. In 1841, he completed his doctoral thesis 'The Concept of Irony' and received his doctorate, but then traveled to Berlin to continue his studies under Schelling.

points.title: 哲学创作的黄金时期
points.description: 从柏林返回哥本哈根后，克尔凯郭尔进入了他创作最 prolific 的时期。1843年，他同时出版了三部重要著作：《或此或彼》、《恐惧与战栗》和《重复》，这些作品奠定了他作为存在主义先驱的地位。他采用多个笔名写作，如维克多·埃雷米塔(Victor Eremita)、约翰内斯·德西伦蒂乌斯(Johannes de Silentio)等，通过不同视角探讨存在的各个层面。1844-1846年间，他发表了《恐惧的概念》、《哲学片段》和《结论性的非科学附言》等重要作品，系统性地批判了黑格尔哲学，提出了'主观真理'、'信仰的飞跃'等核心概念。这一时期，他发展出独特的'间接沟通'方法，通过文学形式表达哲学思想。
points.descriptionEn: After returning from Berlin to Copenhagen, Kierkegaard entered his most prolific creative period. In 1843, he published three major works simultaneously: 'Either/Or', 'Fear and Trembling', and 'Repetition', establishing his position as a pioneer of existentialism. He wrote under multiple pseudonyms such as Victor Eremita and Johannes de Silentio, exploring different aspects of existence from various perspectives. Between 1844-1846, he published important works including 'The Concept of Anxiety', 'Philosophical Fragments', and 'Concluding Unscientific Postscript', systematically critiquing Hegelian philosophy and developing core concepts such as 'subjective truth' and 'leap of faith'. During this period, he developed his unique method of 'indirect communication', expressing philosophical ideas through literary forms.

points.title: 公共论战与危机
points.description: 1846年后，克尔凯郭尔的创作风格发生变化，他更多地参与公共辩论，直接针对当时的教会和知识分子。1848年欧洲革命期间，他表现出对政治的复杂态度，既支持自由又警惕激进变革。1849年，他出版了《致死的疾病》，深入探讨绝望的本质。1850年代，他与丹麦主教马滕森(M.M. Martensen)展开激烈论战，批评国家教会的形式主义和妥协。1854年，他开始针对报纸《祖国》发表一系列文章，批评其编辑海伯格(Heiberg)的哲学观点，这一系列文章后来结集为《瞬间》。这一时期，他的健康状况持续恶化，精神压力增大，创作风格变得更加直接和批判性。
points.descriptionEn: After 1846, Kierkegaard's writing style changed as he became more involved in public debates, directly targeting the church and intellectuals of his time. During the 1848 European revolutions, he showed a complex attitude toward politics, supporting freedom while being wary of radical changes. In 1849, he published 'The Sickness unto Death', deeply exploring the nature of despair. In the 1850s, he engaged in fierce controversies with Danish bishop M.M. Martensen, criticizing the formalism and compromises of the state church. In 1854, he began publishing a series of articles against the newspaper 'The Fatherland', criticizing its editor Heiberg's philosophical views, later collected as 'The Moment'. During this period, his health continued to deteriorate and mental stress increased, making his writing style more direct and critical.

points.title: 最后的日子与遗产
points.description: 1855年，克尔凯郭尔的健康状况急剧恶化，他相信自己被教会和国家迫害。10月，他在街上晕倒，随后被送往医院。在生命的最后几周，他拒绝进食，拒绝接受圣餐，并继续写作。1855年11月11日，他在哥本哈根的弗里德里克斯医院去世，年仅42岁。他的最后作品《上帝的不可改变性》在他去世后出版。克尔凯郭尔的生前作品并未获得广泛认可，但在他去世后，特别是20世纪，他的思想对存在主义、现象学、神学和文学批评产生了深远影响。他被尊为存在主义哲学的奠基人，其关于个体性、选择、焦虑和信仰的思想持续影响着现代哲学和神学思考。
points.descriptionEn: In 1855, Kierkegaard's health deteriorated rapidly, believing he was persecuted by the church and state. In October, he collapsed in the street and was taken to a hospital. In his final weeks, he refused food, rejected communion, and continued writing. On November 11, 1855, he died at Frederiks Hospital in Copenhagen at the age of 42. His final work 'The Immutable Nature of God' was published posthumously. Kierkegaard's works were not widely recognized during his lifetime, but after his death, especially in the 20th century, his ideas had a profound impact on existentialism, phenomenology, theology, and literary criticism. He is revered as the father of existentialist philosophy, and his thoughts on individuality, choice, anxiety, and faith continue to influence modern philosophical and theological thinking.

supporter.zh: 克尔凯郭尔被视为现代存在主义的奠基人，他强调个体选择、主观真理和信仰的飞跃，为后来的哲学开辟了新路径。他勇敢地挑战当时占主导地位的黑格尔哲学体系，捍卫个人自由和真实性的价值。他的作品深刻探讨了人类存在的困境，特别是焦虑、绝望和信仰的本质，为现代人的精神生活提供了重要启示。克尔凯郭尔的思想影响了从萨特到蒂利希等众多哲学家和神学家，他的文学化哲学表达方式也开创了哲学写作的新传统。
supporter.en: Kierkegaard is regarded as the father of modern existentialism, emphasizing individual choice, subjective truth, and the leap of faith, opening new paths for later philosophy. He courageously challenged the dominant Hegelian philosophical system of his time, defending the value of personal freedom and authenticity. His works profoundly explored the dilemmas of human existence, particularly the nature of anxiety, despair, and faith, providing important insights for modern spiritual life. Kierkegaard's ideas influenced numerous philosophers and theologians from Sartre to Tillich, and his literary approach to philosophy pioneered a new tradition in philosophical writing.

critic.zh: 批评者认为克尔凯郭尔的哲学过于个人化和主观，缺乏系统性和普遍适用性。他的宗教立场被指责为非理性主义，对信仰的强调被视为对理性思考的贬低。一些评论家指出他的生活选择，如解除婚约，反映了一种逃避现实而非面对生活的态度。此外，克尔凯郭尔对黑格尔的批判有时被看作是对哲学体系的简单误解，而非真正的哲学对话。他的写作风格复杂多变，使用多个笔名，也被批评为故弄玄虚，增加了理解其思想的难度。
critic.en: Critics argue that Kierkegaard's philosophy is overly personal and subjective, lacking systematicity and universal applicability. His religious stance has been criticized as irrationalist, with his emphasis on faith seen as a denigration of rational thought. Some commentators suggest that his life choices, such as breaking off his engagement, reflect an escapist attitude rather than facing life directly. Additionally, Kierkegaard's critique of Hegel has sometimes been viewed as a simple misunderstanding of philosophical systems rather than genuine philosophical dialogue. His complex writing style, using multiple pseudonyms, has also been criticized as deliberately obscure, increasing the difficulty of understanding his thought.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，克尔凯郭尔被定义为一位跨越哲学与文学边界的思想家。他的存在主义思想在20世纪得到广泛传播，成为应对现代性危机的重要资源。克尔凯郭尔被符号化为'孤独的个体'，在异化的现代社会中寻求真实性和意义。他的概念如'焦虑'、'绝望'和'信仰的飞跃'已成为流行文化中的常用术语，影响从心理学到文学创作的多个领域。尽管他的生前作品未被广泛认可，但死后影响力持续扩大，成为现代思想史上的关键人物，其思想在当代关于身份、信仰和意义的讨论中仍然具有相关性。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Kierkegaard is defined as a thinker who bridged philosophy and literature. His existentialist ideas gained wide dissemination in the 20th century, becoming an important resource for addressing the crisis of modernity. Kierkegaard has been symbolized as the 'solitary individual' seeking authenticity and meaning in an alienated modern society. His concepts such as 'anxiety', 'despair', and 'leap of faith' have become common terms in popular culture, influencing multiple fields from psychology to literary creation. Although his works were not widely recognized during his lifetime, his posthumous influence has continued to expand, making him a key figure in the history of modern thought, with his ideas remaining relevant in contemporary discussions about identity, faith, and meaning.

self.zh: 生活必须向后理解，但必须向前生活。
self.en: Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards.

others.zh: 克尔凯郭尔是所有现代思想家中最伟大的心理学家。
others.en: Kierkegaard is the greatest psychologist of all modern thinkers.
